The LS method encompasses the majority of 1-look-last-slot algorithms on 2x2.  3/4 of a layer is solved on the bottom, with the remaining corner placed somewhere on the top layer. The cube is then solved in one algorithm. Full 1LLS on 2x2 is comprised of CLL, TCLL, and LS. LS is comprised of 486 algorithms in total, divided into 9 subsets (54 algs each) labeled LS-1 through LS-9. These subsets are differentiated by the orientations of the missing last slot piece and of the top layer corner in the empty slot.
Each subset is color coded in this document for ease of use

Each subset has a recognition scheme identical to that of CLL, TCLL+, or TCLL- if needed, but recognizing other patterns may be faster. To use this technique, the bottom layer corner can visually swapped with the white piece, or the case can be recognized by the 3 yellow pieces on top

Additional Notes: You should only explore the algorithms in this method After learning Full EG and TCLL. You will likely find LS1-LS3, the first 3 sets, to be the most useful, as they provide good solutions to average or below average scrambles. LS4-9 are still worthwhile to explore, but they are all cases where CLL can be reached in 3/4 moves, so not every case will save you time.
